g.text: How the VTEP finds remote containers (and why ARP proxying is needed)
Docker fills the kernel tables from its gossip-fed peer database; vxlan0 then answers ARP locally.
A local container gets no VTEP entry: it is a port on br0.
What happens on the first packet
4 frame to that MAC: FDB gives
Without ARP proxying, Container-1's broadcast ARP stops at the L3 boundary between hosts: nobody answers and the failure is silent.
l2miss / l3miss ask the kernel to report lookups it could not answer, so the driver can react.
